abstract.p: Medical image synthesis addresses healthcare data scarcity by generating realistic samples for clinical support systems, AI training, and research. However, the field faces challenges due to the complexity of imaging data with its diverse modalities, characteristics, and disease variations. To produce high-quality images, medical image synthesis typically relies on conditional generation, where labels and annotations serve as essential conditions that provide critical guidance signals during the generation process to control desired semantics and fidelity. However, in the medical domain, labels are often inaccessible due to the high cost of annotation, requirements for clinical expertise, as well as ethical concerns. To address this critical challenge, we propose RepMedGAN, a novel self-supervised representation-guided image generation framework that enhances label-free medical image synthesis by leveraging self-supervised learning representations, enabling high-quality generation across different modalities without requiring labels or annotations. Our framework incorporates a Self-supervised Guidance Module that provides rich semantic knowledge during training and introduces a Guidance Representation Generator to bridge the train-inference disparity. Through extensive evaluation across four diverse medical datasets including brain MRI, chest X-ray, kidney CT, and eye glaucoma images, we demonstrate that RepMedGAN consistently achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple metrics and produces superior-quality medical images.
